sections.html:
Gadsden is the county seat of Etowah County in northeast Alabama, built on both banks of the Coosa River. It lies about 56 miles northeast of Birmingham, 72 miles southeast of Huntsville and 90 miles southwest of Chattanooga, Tennessee.

The southern end of Lookout Mountain rises north of the city center. Gadsden covers about 38.7 square miles, sits at 581 feet, and is the eighteenth-largest city in the state, with an estimated 33,367 residents in 2025.

Because the city is spread across river, valley and mountain edge, the condition and value of a house can change a lot from one side of town to the other.

sections.h2: How did Gadsden's steel and rubber history shape its housing?
sections.html:
Gadsden grew as a river port and heavy-industry city. An early village called Double Springs was founded around 1825, the steamboat Coosa landed in 1845 and the town took the name of Colonel James Gadsden, and the city was incorporated in 1871. By the late 1800s it ranked second only to Mobile among Alabama's commercial centers.

Goodyear Tire and Rubber and Republic Steel anchored the economy into the 1980s. Most major plants closed in the 1970s and 1980s, and the population fell from a peak of 58,088 in 1960 to 33,945 in 2020. In 1991 the city won the All-America City award from the National Civic League.

The city lost population for six straight census counts, which means a seller here is often competing with a lot of other houses for a smaller pool of buyers.

Health care, education and food processing lead the list. The city's 2022 financial report names these as the largest employers.

  • Gadsden Regional Medical Center: 1,312 employees
  • Etowah County Board of Education: 1,275
  • Koch Foods: 1,040
  • Riverview Regional Medical Center: 789
  • Walmart: 750
  • Gadsden City Schools: 693

Gadsden State Community College, the second largest of Alabama's 27 two-year colleges, also sits in the city. The American Community Survey for 2024 puts median household income at $40,345 and says 28.1 percent of residents live below the poverty line, so many owners have limited cash for repairs before a sale.

sections.h2: What are the Gadsden housing numbers?
sections.html:
The 2024 American Community Survey estimates 12,746 households in Gadsden, with 2.53 people per household and 16,513 housing units. That is about 3,700 more units than households, so some of those units are vacant.

The census median age is 38.6, and 15.5 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher. With incomes at that level, a seller should weigh carefully how much a repair will add to the price a buyer can afford.

  • Estimated households: 12,746 (2024 ACS)
  • Housing units: 16,513
  • Median household income: $40,345
  • Poverty rate: 28.1 percent

sections.h2: What is Gadsden's climate, and how does it affect houses?
sections.html:
Gadsden has a humid subtropical climate. January averages 41.3 degrees and July averages 80.6, with 60 to 61 days a year reaching 90 degrees or more. The temperature has touched 106 degrees, in June 2012, and dropped to minus 6 in January 1985.

Rain is abundant, with January and February the wettest months, while snow is rare. Heat and humidity strain air conditioning and roofs, and freezing nights occur on roughly 60 days a year, so older plumbing in unheated spaces can be at risk.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit work in Gadsden?
sections.html:
Gadsden is served by Interstate 59 and Interstate 759, plus U.S. Highways 411, 431 and 278. The city has a trolley system, Greyhound service and the Northeast Alabama Regional Airport, and freight rail runs on Norfolk Southern and the Alabama and Tennessee River Railway.

Birmingham is about 56 miles away, so houses near the I-59 exits are within reach of that job market.

Gadsden City Schools runs fourteen schools: eight elementary, three middle, one high school, and two specialty schools. Gadsden City High School opened for the 2006 to 2007 school year after three older city high schools merged.

Etowah County Schools has its headquarters in Gadsden but does not serve addresses inside the city limits, which matters when you describe school zoning to a buyer.

sections.h2: How do Etowah County property taxes work for a seller?
sections.html:
The Etowah County Revenue Commissioner values property, and the county's tax FAQ lists the yearly schedule. Taxes are due October 1 and delinquent on January 1, and unpaid bills are turned over to the probate court in February with a tax sale in May.

The county also says taxes follow the property, so a buyer pays any past-due amounts even if they were incurred under a prior owner. That is why title companies check tax status before closing.

October 1Tax due

AprilAdvertised for sale

Unpaid taxes can be redeemed within three years of a tax sale by paying taxes, interest, fees and penalties at 12 percent a year. Owner-occupied property falls in Class III, assessed at 10 percent of value.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in Gadsden?
sections.html: The state recordation tax is 50 cents per $500 of value under Alabama Code 40-22-1, so a $100,000 house owes $100 in deed tax. Etowah County advises buyers to record the deed with the probate office and then assess the property with the Revenue Commissioner, bringing the deed.

sections.h2: What should a Gadsden seller do after the sale closes?
sections.html:
Etowah County's tax office tells new owners to record the deed and then assess the property, and it asks owners to report address changes in writing. As the seller, keep your closing statement and the tax receipt, in case a question about the tax year comes up later.

  • Keep a copy of the recorded deed and settlement statement
  • Confirm the tax year was prorated correctly
  • Send the Revenue Commissioner your new mailing address in writing

The county notes that it is not required to mail tax notices, and that owners remain responsible for the tax whether or not a statement arrives.

sections.h2: What are a Gadsden seller's options?
sections.html:
You can list the house, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer. Listing may reach the most buyers, but financed buyers need an appraisal and an inspection, and a house that needs work may not clear both.

  • List with an agent when the house is in good shape and you can wait
  • Sell privately if you have time and can handle the paperwork
  • Take a cash offer if the house needs repairs, has tax or title problems, or is inherited

Cash Home Buyers purchases Gadsden houses as they stand, and you can turn the offer down.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Gadsden house with unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid amount is normally paid from the sale proceeds at closing, because taxes follow the property. Ask the title company for a payoff figure.

faqs.q: When does Etowah County turn unpaid taxes over for sale?
faqs.a: The county says taxes are due October 1 and delinquent January 1. Delinquent accounts go to the probate court in February and are advertised in April, with a sale in May.

faqs.q: How much is the deed tax on a Gadsden sale?
faqs.a: Alabama charges 50 cents per $500 of value, so a $120,000 sale owes $120 in deed tax. A recording fee is added.
Major industries such as Republic Steel and Goodyear closed in the 1970s and 1980s, and the population dropped from 58,088 in 1960 to 33,945 in 2020.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Gadsden house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer takes it in its current condition. Retail buyers using loans often need the house to meet lender standards.

faqs.q: Do I need to live in Gadsden to sell my house here?
faqs.a: No. Many owners live elsewhere, and the sale can be handled by mail or through a title company.
